author: Temminck, 1825
habitat: 해안 바위 지대, 섬의 바위 능선과 맨땅

months.note: 국내에서 기록된 달이다(2008년 1월 포항, 2009년 5월 어청도·10월 가거도).

summary: 2008년 1월 경북 포항에서 처음 기록된 길잃은새로, 2009년 5월 어청도와 10월 가거도에서도 관찰되었다. 북아프리카에서 중동·중앙아시아를 거쳐 몽골과 중국 서부까지 사막과 건조한 초원에서 번식하며, 아시아 개체군은 모두 남쪽으로 옮겨 가 겨울을 난다. 주로 맨땅에서 개미·딱정벌레와 그 애벌레를 잡아먹고, 때로는 날아오르며 곤충을 낚아챈다.

points.en: black face and throat joining the black wings at the shoulder (male)
tail almost entirely black, white only at the base

sexes.male: 윗면은 모래빛 갈색이고 흰 눈썹선이 있으며, 얼굴과 멱의 검은색이 목옆을 따라 검은 날개와 이어진다.
sexes.female: 얼굴과 멱이 검지 않고 담황색이며, 윗면은 수컷보다 흐린 회갈색, 날개는 흑갈색이다. 꼬리가 거의 검은 점은 수컷과 같다.

young: 어린새는 암컷과 비슷하지만 윗면 깃 가운데가 희고 끝이 갈색이어서 얼룩져 보이며, 멱과 가슴에도 담황갈색 깃 끝이 있다. 첫 겨울 수컷은 멱의 검은 깃 끝이 희어 검은색이 일부 가려진다.

art.subject: Desert Wheatear (Oenanthe deserti), adult male in spring, a vagrant on a Korean coastal dune: crown, nape, mantle and scapulars pale sandy-buff; a whitish supercilium; face, chin and throat solid black, the black continuing down the sides of the neck to join the black wing at the shoulder; wing coverts and flight feathers black, the inner wing coverts edged white, forming a whitish line between the sandy scapulars and the black wing; breast and belly creamy buff-white; rump and uppertail coverts white; tail almost entirely black, with white only at the base. Bill black; eye dark; legs black.
art.pose: perched upright on a low sandy hummock, side view
art.scene: sandy coastal dune with sparse dry grass behind a Korean beach in early spring (March–April), soft clear light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male spring, side view perched upright on a low sandy hummock: pale sandy-buff crown, nape and back, white supercilium, black face, chin and throat continuing down the neck side to join the black wings, creamy buff-white breast and belly, whitish rump, tail almost entirely black with white only at the base, slender black bill, black legs
adult female, side view perched upright: grey-brown upperparts, buffish-white underparts with no black on the throat, darker brown wings, whitish rump, almost entirely dark tail, slender dark bill

adult male, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, sandy-buff head and back contrasting with black wings, whitish rump, black tail with white only at its base
art.build: A small, compact wheatear about the size of a sparrow, slightly smaller and shorter-legged than Isabelline Wheatear, with a rounded head and upright stance; perches on low hummocks and drops to the ground for insects. Bill black, slender, shorter than the head. Legs black, moderately long. Tail square, looking all black above a white rump. In flight the black wings contrast with the sandy back and the white rump with the black tail.
avoid: Do not paint a white tail with a black inverted T (Northern and Isabelline Wheatears); in Desert Wheatear the tail is almost entirely black.
Do not separate the black throat from the black wings with a pale band; in the male they join along the neck side.
Do not paint a grey or blue-grey back; the male's crown and back are sandy-buff.
Do not paint a black crown or cap.
Do not paint black scapulars; the scapulars are sandy-buff like the back, and only the wing coverts and flight feathers are black.
